Chapter 9.4

How is energy conserved?

Forms of energy, energy conversions, and why the total never changes

A rollercoaster car climbs once and never gets a push again. Where does the rest of the ride come from?

Learning Objectives

What you will be able to do by the end of this lesson

  • Name the different forms of energy and give an example of each.
  • Describe the energy conversions that take place during a rollercoaster ride.
  • State the principle of the conservation of energy.
  • Explain why total energy is made up of useful energy and energy transferred to the surroundings.

Learn
  • Different forms of energy exist around us, and every one of them is measured in joules.
  • A device does not hold one form of energy. It takes one form in and gives another form out.The fan takes electricity in and gives movement out. The lamp takes electricity in and gives light out.
  • Chemical potential energy is stored energy. It is released when we use it.
Key Facts
  • Electrical, sound, light, heat and chemical potential energy are all forms of energy.
  • The SI unit of energy is the joule (J).

Core concept

What forms does energy take?

The forms look completely different, yet all of them are measured in the same unit!

Learn
  • Electrical energy is used to power devices like the television and the electric fan.
  • Sound energy enables us to listen to our favourite music. Light energy allows us to see things, while heat energy enables us to warm up our food.
  • Chemical potential energy in the food we eat is converted to kinetic energy when we move about.The energy in your lunch does not stay in your lunch. It becomes the energy you run on.
  • The SI unit of energy is the joule (J). Energy can be converted from one form to another.One unit covers all of them. Heat, light, sound and movement are all counted in joules.
Key Facts
  • The SI unit of energy is the joule (J), the same unit used for work done.
  • Energy is converted from one form to another. It is never used up.
  • Chemical potential energy is stored energy. Kinetic energy is the energy of movement.
Test

A girl listens to music on her phone while she dances. Which conversion is taking place in the headphones?

How does the energy change around the track?

Let's find out how the energy changes, from the highest point to the lowest

Rollercoaster Tour1 / 6
1Press Next stop to follow the car from the top of the first hill to the bottom.
Stop 1 of 6 : Point A, the highest point
Learn
  • At the highest point, A, the car has maximum gravitational potential energy.
  • As the car moves down from A to B, gravitational potential energy of the car is converted to kinetic energy. When the car moves up again from B to C, some kinetic energy of the car is converted to gravitational potential energy.Going down trades height for speed. Going up trades speed back for height.
  • At the lowest point, D, the car has maximum kinetic energy.
Key Facts
  • Gravitational potential energy is largest where the car is highest.
  • Kinetic energy is largest where the car is lowest and moving fastest.

Core concept

What does it mean to say energy is conserved?

The forms change all the way round the track. The total does NOT!

Learn
  • During the ride, the total energy of the car remains constant. We say that energy is conserved.Add up everything the car has at any moment and you always get the same number, wherever it is on the track.
  • This means that energy is not created or destroyed, but transferred from one object to another, or converted from one form to another.Energy never appears from nowhere and never disappears. It only moves, or changes into a different form.
  • The various forms of energy at each point will always add up to the total energy.
  • In an ideal situation, when the car moves from the highest point, A, to the lowest point, D, all gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy of the car when it reaches the bottom of the track.Ideal means we are ignoring friction and air resistance for a moment, so every joule of height becomes a joule of speed.
Key Facts
  • Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be transferred or converted.
  • The energy conversion from A to D is gravitational potential energy at A to kinetic energy at D.
  • In an ideal situation the total energy at any time remains constant.
Test

A student says the car's energy is used up by the time it reaches the bottom. What is wrong with this?

📓Now complete your notes: Section C: The conservation of energyWrite the conservation of energy statement. Use the exact words from the Learn tab.
Core concept

Why is the real ride not the ideal one?

In reality some of the energy leaves the car altogether, and it never comes back!

Learn
  • In any situation, the total energy at any time remains constant.
  • In general, total energy is made up of useful energy and energy transferred to the surroundings.Some of the energy does the job you wanted. The rest escapes into the air around it. Add the two and you have all of it.
  • In reality, energy may be transferred to the surroundings as heat, sound and light.Rub your hands together and they get warm. The rollercoaster does the same thing against its rails, and the energy leaves as heat and noise.
  • This is why the second hill of a rollercoaster is always lower than the first.
Key Facts
  • Total energy is made up of useful energy and energy transferred to the surroundings.
  • Energy transferred to the surroundings is still energy. It has not been destroyed, only spread out.
  • This is why the second hill of a rollercoaster is always lower than the first.
Test

Why is the second hill of a real rollercoaster always lower than the first?

Where is energy leaving to the surroundings?

Learn
  • Energy transferred to the surroundings has not been destroyed. It has been spread out into the air, the rails and the ground.The energy is still there. It is just so thinly spread that nothing can use it any more.
  • Heat, sound and light are the three ways this happens.
  • Total energy is made up of useful energy and energy transferred to the surroundings.
Key Facts
  • Energy cannot be destroyed, only transferred or converted.
  • Saving energy means keeping more of it useful, not stopping it from disappearing.
